Hi Camila,

Thanks for taking this on. We're starting contracting for our pilot with Redwood and Legal has a few targeted asks to add to the DPA before we proceed. I attached our redlines (Clearmed_DPA_redlines_v1.pdf). High-level asks below — can you confirm which we can accept as written vs. where we need operational proof?

Key items we need validated:
- Explicit commitment that Redwood will not use our data to improve, retrain, or fine-tune any models used to serve Clearmed (we call this a no-model-improvement / no-derivative rights commitment).
- Clear output/ownership language: Clearmed retains all rights to prompts and outputs generated by our users; Redwood must not assert derivative IP over those outputs.
- Subprocessor disclosure and evidence of gating for model-training-scope: a current inventory and an ops attestation process for any changes.
- Data residency options for EU customers and a mechanism to route EU traffic to EU-hosted instances (if requested).
- KMS and key control options (bring-your-own-key preferred) or explain onshore KMS alternatives.
- SOC 2 report, recent penetration test summary, and an evidence pack showing the operational steps for a "no-model-improvement" implementation (how prefix/KV caching and ephemeral storage are handled).

We'd like to get this resolved before our legal review next week. Is it possible to get a consolidated response + evidence pack by EOD Thursday? Also looping in Contracts.

Thanks,
Sara Lopez
Head of Security & Privacy
Clearmed AI

Hi Sara — great to meet you (virtually). Thanks for the redlines and clear list. We're aligned on the timeline and can provide both contractual language and the operational evidence you asked for. High-level response below and we'll attach a short subprocessor brief and an evidence checklist for your ops review (redwood-subprocessors-brief.pdf; ops-evidence-checklist.xlsx).

1) No-model-improvement commitment
- We can commit to a strict operational path for customers who require no-model-improvement (we typically call this the "model-improvement opt-out"). Contractually we can add a clause that Redwood will not use Clearmed data for model training or improvement for models serving your tenant.
- Operationally we implement this via routing to non-adaptive serving pools, explicit KV/prefix cache controls, and exclusion filters. We'll include the engineering notes in the evidence checklist.

2) Output / prompt ownership
- Redwood does not retain ownership of customer prompts/outputs. We are comfortable with language that rights to outputs remain with the customer; we will not assert derivative IP. We'll propose specific DPA wording in a redline set.

3) Subprocessors / attestation
- We'll provide our current subprocessor inventory and a short description of gating controls for training-scope changes. For customers requesting stronger assurances we can show a signed attestation every time a training-relevant subprocessor is added. See attached brief.

4) Data residency / KMS
- EU routing: we support region pinning for production tenants and can route EU traffic to EU-hosted instances (configurable at onboarding).
- KMS: we support BYOK for Dedicated and Private deployments. For Hosted customers we can discuss an onshore KMS arrangement or a dedicated key-holding option.

5) Audit evidence
- SOC 2 report and a recent pentest summary can be shared under an NDA / secure link. Ops evidence checklist includes the specific artifacts we can provide (diagram of dataflows, KV eviction policy, retention controls).

Next steps: I'll have David (ops lead) and Kimberly (legal) prepare the evidence pack and a DPA redline. Can we push for a short ops call to walk through the checklist? I'm free Thursday 10-11am or Friday 1-3pm PT.

Best,
Camila Reyes

Camila / David — quick notes for the DPA redline and evidence pack. Please include these items in the proposed language and have ops annotate the evidence checklist where appropriate.

- Wording: prefer "Redwood will not use Customer Data to train, fine-tune, or improve any models that are used to serve Customer (including derivative models)". That phrasing avoids ambiguity between passive telemetry and active model improvement.
- Outputs: add explicit line that customer retains all rights to prompts and outputs and that Redwood assigns no derivative rights to outputs generated by customer interactions.
- Attestation cadence: for customers requiring a higher bar, propose quarterly attestation of subprocessor changes that could affect training scope (with a notification window and right to object).
- KMS: for Hosted customers push for BYOK or dedicated-key escrow onshore; if that's not feasible, ask for clear technical constraints and an SLA for key-separation enforcement.
- Evidence scope: include SOC 2 + pen test + a short runbook that shows how ephemeral KV/prefix caches are zeroed for opt-out tenants and how routing pins are enforced. Ops should mark which artifacts are shareable vs. NDA-only.

If we can't close by Thursday EOD, propose we commit to a consolidated redline + evidence link by Friday EOD instead.

-Kimberly
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
